rugby_historian.text: Ask me about the Sevens. I'll answer, and then I'll tell you the story of my knee.

then.text: Melrose RFC was short of money, so in 1883 Ned Haig, a local butcher and a club member, suggested a tournament of seven-a-side games, played in a single afternoon. The first Melrose Sevens was held in the spring of 1883.
The idea spread across the world. It's the main format of rugby for the Olympic Games now, and it's all because a butcher needed some money.
The ground is called the Greenyards, and the Melrose Sevens is still held there every spring, so the whole town turns out in its best.

Seven-a-side is faster and more open than the fifteen-man game, with more space and fewer places to hide. A match is two halves of seven minutes. It is the most exhausting fourteen minutes of your life, and you'll want a pie after.
Come back any time. History keeps.

rugby_landlord.text: Welcome to the clubhouse. The bar's open, the soup's hot and the quiz is cold. Fancy a go?

else.text: No rush. We've got the whole of the Borders to talk about.
